Established causes are distinguished from hypotheses, with competing explanations investigated when relevant. The responsible layer owns the guarantee, has the information to enforce it, and covers affected paths without inappropriate responsibilities; it need not be the deepest or most shared layer. The correction addresses that mechanism, including necessary callers and tests, while preserving supported behavior and respecting the task contract and exclusions. A coherent correction that reduces special cases is preferred; diff size is a cost, not the objective. Existing patterns are evidence, not proof of sound design. Validation covers the original failure, relevant neighboring cases, preserved behavior, and whether affected paths use the repaired boundary. Expected results come from the contract rather than the patch's assumptions. Failed attempts or recurring findings require new evidence distinguishing implementation errors from an incorrect diagnosis before another workaround is justified. A mitigation leaves its residual cause actionable or blocked; passing tests alone does not establish resolution. Explanations are proportional to uncertainty and risk; an established local defect does not require an architecture exercise.

findings.title: Preserve case when normalizing account identifiers
findings.evidence: id.cjs:2 adds toLowerCase(), violating README.md:1 and the identifier criterion. A read-only diagnostic demonstrated normalizeId('  AbC  ') returns 'abc', lookupKey returns 'account:abc', and receipt returns {id:'abc'}. lookupKey('AbC') equals lookupKey('abc'), collapsing distinct case-sensitive account identifiers. Both affected callers use normalizeId in callers.cjs:2-3. Remove the lowercasing at this shared normalization boundary while preserving trim(). Existing check.cjs:5-7 already asserts the required case-preserving behavior.

acceptance.evidence: Inspected the complete changed scope and both callers. Whitespace stripping remains, but case preservation fails in normalization, lookup keys, and receipts, as demonstrated by the diagnostic above. check.cjs:5-7 covers this contract. These are reviewer diagnostics and source evidence; controller validation evidence was not supplied.

label.cjs:1 independently conditions prefix and suffix, preserving the original behavior for supported display flags. A read-only diagnostic returned 'X', 'X]', '[X', and '[X]' for (false,false), (false,true), (true,false), and (true,true), respectively. check.cjs:8 covers all four combinations. These are reviewer diagnostics and source evidence; controller validation evidence was not supplied.

findings.title: Normalization changes case-sensitive account identifiers
findings.evidence: Line 2 calls toLowerCase() after trim(). README.md states that identifiers are case-sensitive and normalization preserves all characters except surrounding whitespace. callers.cjs uses normalizeId for both lookup keys and receipts, so '  AbC  ' becomes 'account:abc' and {id:'abc'} instead of the 'AbC' values required by check.cjs lines 5–7.

acceptance.evidence: id.cjs line 2 lowercases normalized values. The lookup key and receipt both use that function, violating the case-preservation contract.
label.cjs line 1 independently selects the opening bracket from prefix and the closing bracket from suffix. It produces the expected output for all four combinations in check.cjs line 8.
